items.question_text: You deployed an App Engine application using gcloud app deploy, but it did not deploy to the intended project. You want to find out why this happened and where the application deployed. What should you do?
items.solution_text: The gcloud CLI uses the active configuration context to determine the target project if no --project flag is provided during deployment. Running gcloud config list displays the current core settings, including the default project ID, allowing you to identify why the application deployed to an unexpected location. While app.yaml may contain a project ID in some Standard environment cases, it is ignored in Flexible environments and often absent, making the CLI configuration check the definitive diagnostic step.

choices.text: Check the app.yaml file for your application and check project settings.
Check the web-application.xml file for your application and check project settings.
Go to Deployment Manager and review settings for deployment of applications.
Go to Cloud Shell and run gcloud config list to review the Google Cloud configuration used for deployment.

items.question_text: You want to configure 10 Compute Engine instances for availability when maintenance occurs. Your requirements state that these instances should attempt to automatically restart if they crash. Also, the instances should be highly available including during system maintenance. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To meet the requirement for automatic restart upon crash, you must enable the 'Automatic Restart' setting on the instance template. To ensure high availability during system maintenance without downtime, you must set the 'On-host maintenance' policy to 'Migrate VM instance', which triggers live migration instead of termination.
Creating these instances within an instance group ensures they are managed as a scalable and highly available unit.

choices.text: Create an instance template for the instances. Set the 'Automatic Restart' to on. Set the 'On-host maintenance' to Migrate VM instance. Add the instance template to an instance group.
Create an instance template for the instances. Set 'Automatic Restart' to off. Set 'On-host maintenance' to Terminate VM instances. Add the instance template to an instance group.
Create an instance group for the instances. Set the 'Autohealing' health check to healthy (HTTP).
Create an instance group for the instance. Verify that the 'Advanced creation options' setting for 'do not retry machine creation' is set to off.

items.question_text: You host a static website on Cloud Storage. Recently, you began to include links to PDF files on this site. Currently, when users click on the links to these PDF files, their browsers prompt them to save the file onto their local system. Instead, you want the clicked PDF files to be displayed within the browser window directly, without prompting the user to save the file locally. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Browsers determine how to handle downloaded files based on the Content-Type header sent by the server. Setting this metadata to 'application/pdf' signals the browser that the file is a PDF, enabling it to render the document in the built-in viewer instead of triggering a download.

Labels (Option D) are for organization and do not affect HTTP headers, while CDN (Option A) and public access settings (Option B) handle performance and permissions, respectively, not content rendering behavior.

choices.text: Enable Cloud CDN on the website frontend.
Enable 'Share publicly' on the PDF file objects.
Set Content-Type metadata to application/pdf on the PDF file objects.
Add a label to the storage bucket with a key of Content-Type and value of application/pdf.

items.question_text: You have a virtual machine that is currently configured with 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of memory. It is running out of memory. You want to upgrade the virtual machine to have 8 GB of memory. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
In Google Compute Engine, modifying the memory allocation of a virtual machine requires stopping the instance first, as live resizing is not supported for standard machines.
Option D is correct because it follows the mandatory stop-edit-start workflow without unnecessarily changing other resources.
Option C is incorrect because switching to an n1-standard-8 machine type would drastically increase vCPUs and memory beyond the specific requirement of 8 GB, leading to overprovisioning.

choices.text: Rely on live migration to move the workload to a machine with more memory.
Use gcloud to add metadata to the VM. Set the key to required-memory-size and the value to 8 GB.
Stop the VM, change the machine type to n1-standard-8, and start the VM.
Stop the VM, increase the memory to 8 GB, and start the VM.

items.question_text:
You have production and test workloads that you want to deploy on Compute Engine. Production VMs need to be in a different subnet than the test VMs. All the
VMs must be able to reach each other over Internal IP without creating additional routes. You need to set up VPC and the 2 subnets. Which configuration meets these requirements?
items.solution_text: Google Cloud VPCs are global resources where all subnets within the same network must have non-overlapping CIDR ranges, making option B invalid. Subnets in the same VPC automatically route to each other via internal IP without requiring manual configuration, satisfying the connectivity requirement. Option A correctly implements a single VPC with distinct, non-overlapping subnets in different regions to separate production and test workloads while maintaining seamless communication.

choices.text: Create a single custom VPC with 2 subnets. Create each subnet in a different region and with a different CIDR range.
Create a single custom VPC with 2 subnets. Create each subnet in the same region and with the same CIDR range.
Create 2 custom VPCs, each with a single subnet. Create each subnet in a different region and with a different CIDR range.
Create 2 custom VPCs, each with a single subnet. Create each subnet in the same region and with the same CIDR range.
